redFlags.why: This is a fake web address disguised to look like a real bank.
Real banks will not give you a two-hour deadline to unlock your account.
Threatening to freeze your money is a common trick to make you panic.
Using capital letters to say your account is locked creates sudden fear.

advice: Do not click the link or enter any personal details.
If you bank with Brightway, call the number on the back of your bank card to check your account.
You can forward scam text messages to 7726 for free to report them, then delete the message.

redFlags.phrase: Your supply will be disconnected tomorrow at 9am
redFlags.why: UK energy companies must follow strict rules and never cut you off overnight by text.
Scammers rush you into paying before you have time to check if the bill is real.
This web address looks unusual and is likely a fake payment page.
Energy companies use freephone or landline numbers for customer service, not mobile numbers.
Uses alarming capital letters to make you panic.

advice: Do not click the link or call the mobile number in the message.
Check your energy account by calling the number on a real paper bill, or by logging in through your usual website or app.
You can forward scam texts to 7726 for free to report them to your mobile provider.
